cheap_test_done: Cheap test 1, 25 Sept 2026 (VX-CT03, ciphers/na-oldenbarnevelt-2442-1605/scripts/solve_digit_subst.py). Two independent blind transcription passes of the three cipher blocks disagreed heavily (char-level agreement: block A folio 54 80.9%, block B folio 55 72.7%, block C1 folio 56 first passage 70.3%, block C2 folio 56 second passage 49.7% -- below the transcription brief's 60% gate, held back for a fresh pass/crops, not used here). Blocks A/B/C1 were reconciled by sequence-aligning the two passes and, on mismatch, preferring whichever candidate decoded to a real word in a period Spanish corpus (Don Quijote I, 1605) under the digit key established from clean dictionary hits in block A alone (secretario, Francisco, palabras, particulares, son, Dios all confirm a=4, e=8, i=3, o=7, u=2); only block A (68 tokens, N=325 sign-stream characters, 156 digits over K=7 distinct symbols, 66% of tokens resolved to high/medium confidence) was carried into the actual test, since B/C1's own resolution rate was near 50%. Target run (8 restarts, order-4 char n-gram): best candidate is FAIL on tools/judge_plaintext.py's language check (score -1.26 vs the real-text 5th percentile -0.855; clears the null/gibberish threshold at -1.944) but PASSES word-cover (0.729 > 0.5 min, vs 0.905 real-text median); qualitatively it recovers clear, unforced Spanish ("no he podido allar para enuiar mismas palabras que son particulares", "su condicion", "dios gguie como sea") consistent with the same key found in block A's cleanest words. Matched control (same N=325, K=7, same solver, 3 seeds, clean crib letters from a held-out Don Quijote passage): 100% digit-position recovery every seed -- a ceiling effect (CLAUDE.md rule 3's own caveat: a control already at ceiling has no headroom to show a gain). A second, noise-matched control (same N, K, seeds, but with the SAME share of crib letters (37.3%, matching block A's own low-confidence-token letter share) corrupted to a wrong letter before solving) still recovered 100% of digit positions every seed -- so the target's language-check FAIL is not explained by ordinary single-character letter-substitution noise at the rate block A's transcription actually has; the more likely explanation is that some of the disputed tokens are wrong in a more structural way (wrong character count / segmentation, not just a wrong letter value -- several A/B disagreements differ in length, e.g. token 20 'A=8n234r'(6 chars) vs 'B=4a25.'(5 chars)), which this noise model does not simulate. Conclusion: the digit-substitution design is real and the key is right where transcription is solid; the FAIL is a transcription-quality result, not a design-level negative, and the fix is a further (glyph-crop-level) pass on block A's 23 remaining low-confidence tokens and a fresh pass entirely on block C2, not a bigger solver. Not promoted past this cheap test (breadth-lane brief: one test, then stop).
